title: Iraq invades Kuwait
description: Iraqi forces invade Kuwait, putting Kuwaiti and regional Gulf supply at risk

title: Lehman Brothers collapses
description: Financial crisis escalates into a global demand-destruction shock

title: US-led invasion of Iraq begins
description: Invasion of a major producer; heavily telegraphed for months beforehand

title: Libyan civil war begins and production halts
description: Uprising escalates into civil war, removing Libyan output from the market

title: OPEC declines to cut production
description: OPEC opts not to reduce output despite falling prices, signalling a defence of market share

title: OPEC agrees to cut production
description: First coordinated cut since 2008, ending the market-share strategy

title: US withdraws from JCPOA and reimposes Iran sanctions
description: US exits the nuclear deal, signalling restoration of oil sanctions on Iran

title: US sanctions on PDVSA
description: Sanctions target Venezuelan state oil company exports

title: Attack on Saudi Abqaiq and Khurais facilities
description: Aerial attack temporarily removes a large share of Saudi processing capacity

title: US strike kills Qassem Soleimani
description: Sharp US-Iran escalation raising fears of regional conflict and Hormuz risk

title: OPEC+ talks collapse and price war begins
description: Russia and Saudi Arabia fail to agree cuts, triggering a market-share price war into collapsing demand

title: WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic
description: Global demand destruction as economies shut down; confounded with the OPEC+ price war

title: OPEC+ agrees record production cut
description: Historic ~9.7 million b/d cut agreed in response to pandemic oversupply. NOTE: EIA dates the agreement 15 April - verify exact date

title: Ever Given blocks the Suez Canal
description: Container ship grounds and blocks a chokepoint carrying roughly 10% of seaborne oil trade

title: Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine
description: Invasion raises prospect of sanctions on and disruption to a top-three global producer; heavily anticipated

title: Nord Stream pipelines sabotaged
description: Multiple ruptures detected in Nord Stream 1 and 2, severing a major Russia-Europe gas route

title: EU seaborne embargo and G7 price cap take effect
description: EU ban on seaborne Russian crude plus a $60 G7 price cap enter into force

title: OPEC+ announces surprise voluntary cuts
description: Unscheduled announcement of additional voluntary production cuts

title: Hamas attack on Israel and onset of Gaza war
description: Major Middle East escalation raising regional conflict and supply-risk premia

title: Houthi attacks disrupt Red Sea shipping
description: Attacks on commercial shipping divert traffic from Bab el-Mandeb; crude flows through the chokepoint fell ~18% in Dec 2023 and over 50% in early 2024

title: Operation Desert Storm air campaign begins
description: US-led coalition begins the air war on Iraq after the Jan 15 UN withdrawal deadline; puts Iraqi and Kuwaiti crude and the wider Gulf risk premium in play. DRAFT coding, awaiting Joe's review.

title: Operation Desert Fox airstrikes on Iraq
description: Four days of US/UK airstrikes on Iraqi military and WMD targets during the UNSCOM inspections crisis; Iraqi exports were sanction-limited then, so expected supply disruption was moderate. DRAFT coding.

title: September 11 terrorist attacks
description: Coordinated attacks on the US; the oil channel is mainly a demand and risk shock (aviation collapse, recession fear) rather than a producer supply loss. Joe may reclassify type as demand_shock. DRAFT coding.

title: Israel-Hezbollah (Second Lebanon) war begins
description: Hezbollah cross-border raid triggers a 34-day war; neither party is an oil producer, so the channel is a regional risk premium and fear of wider Iran involvement. Sourced to the UN resolution that ended the war. DRAFT coding.

title: Russia-Georgia war
description: Russia (a top-three crude producer) invades Georgia, the transit state for the BTC pipeline carrying Caspian crude to market; pipeline and transit risk is the oil channel. DRAFT coding.

title: Saudi-led intervention in Yemen (Operation Decisive Storm)
description: Saudi Arabia, the world's largest crude exporter, leads a coalition air campaign in Yemen; the channel is Saudi involvement plus Bab-el-Mandeb transit risk near the Red Sea. DRAFT coding.

title: Gulf of Oman tanker attacks
description: Two oil/product tankers struck near the Strait of Hormuz amid US-Iran tensions; attribution to Iran was asserted but contested (hence medium confidence). Channel is chokepoint and shipping risk. DRAFT coding.

title: Iran's first direct missile and drone strike on Israel
description: Iran launches 300+ drones and missiles at Israel in retaliation for the April 1 Damascus consulate strike; largely telegraphed for about two weeks, so surprise is low despite the scale. DRAFT coding.

title: Iran's October ballistic-missile strike on Israel
description: Iran fires about 180 ballistic missiles at Israel after the killing of Hezbollah's leader; the direct Iran-Israel exchange lifts the Middle East war premium and Hormuz risk. DRAFT coding.

title: Israel-Iran war onset (Operation Rising Lion)
description: Israel launches a wide air campaign against Iran's nuclear and military sites, opening a 12-day war; a direct attack on a major OPEC producer with acute Strait of Hormuz risk. DRAFT coding.

title: EU embargo on Iranian oil
description: Council Decision 2012/35/CFSP bans import purchase and transport of Iranian crude; phased with full effect 1 July 2012; heavily telegraphed for weeks beforehand. DRAFT coding.

title: US ends all Iran oil sanction waivers
description: Pompeo announces no renewal of significant-reduction exceptions for eight buyers of Iranian crude; markets had expected extensions; ~1 mb/d at stake. DRAFT coding.

title: US financial sanctions on Venezuela (EO 13808)
description: Executive Order 13808 bars dealings in new debt of PDVSA and the Venezuelan government; first financial-sector strike at the oil state; effective 25 Aug 2017. DRAFT coding.

title: Saudi Arabia suspends oil shipments through Bab el-Mandeb
description: After Houthi attacks on two Saudi tankers Riyadh halts all crude transit through the strait (~500-700 kb/d) until safety is restored. DRAFT coding.

title: Iran seizes British tanker Stena Impero in Hormuz
description: IRGC seizes UK-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz at the peak of the 2019 tanker crisis; direct state interference with transit through the top oil chokepoint. DRAFT coding.

title: Tanker Bridgeton strikes Iranian mine in first Earnest Will convoy
description: Reflagged Kuwaiti supertanker hits IRGC mine near Farsi Island during first US-escorted convoy of the Tanker War. NOTE: daily Brent history begins mid-1987 so the estimation window may be too short - engine may drop this event; approving it is still safe. DRAFT coding.

title: Colonial Pipeline ransomware shutdown
description: Ransomware attack shuts the largest US refined-products pipeline (~45% of East Coast fuel) for five days; cyber rather than kinetic; products more than crude. DRAFT coding.

title: Houthi drone and missile attack on Ras Tanura
description: Drone strikes the worlds largest oil loading facility plus Aramco Dhahran compound; minimal physical damage but first direct hit at the heart of Saudi export infrastructure since Abqaiq. DRAFT coding.

title: OPEC Jakarta meeting raises production ceiling 10%
description: Conference of 26 Nov - 1 Dec 1997 lifts ceiling from 25 to 27.5 mb/d into the teeth of the Asian crisis; textbook pro-cyclical error preceding the 1998 price collapse. Dated to close of conference. DRAFT coding.

title: OPEC ratifies 1.7 mb/d production cut
description: Vienna meeting ratifies the Hague framework (agreed ~10 days earlier so partially telegraphed) totalling ~2.1 mb/d with non-OPEC; launched the 1999 price recovery. DRAFT coding.

title: OPEC+ announces 2 mb/d production cut
description: First in-person meeting since 2020 cuts quotas by 2 mb/d - largest since the pandemic - over explicit US objection; ~1 mb/d had been rumored so partially anticipated. DRAFT coding.

title: Thailand floats the baht - Asian crisis begins
description: Bank of Thailand abandons the dollar peg; baht falls 15-20% at once; the discrete dateable trigger of the Asian financial crisis and the 1997-98 oil demand collapse. DRAFT coding.

title: US Iran and Libya Sanctions Act signed
description: Clinton signs ILSA: sanctions on foreign firms investing >$20M/yr in Iranian (or >$40M Libyan) petroleum development; first US secondary-sanctions strike at partner-country energy investment. DRAFT coding.

title: US NDAA sanctions on Central Bank of Iran
description: NDAA Sec 1245 signed: blocks CBI and threatens sanctions on third-country banks settling Iranian oil trades - the financial chokehold on Iranian exports. Clusters with the EU embargo 23 days later; keep-first rule applies. DRAFT coding.

title: SWIFT disconnects Iranian banks
description: Unprecedented: SWIFT cuts 30 Iranian banks from international payments messaging under EU directive - the plumbing-level enforcement of the oil embargo. DRAFT coding.

title: US blocks all Venezuelan government property (EO 13884)
description: Full asset freeze on the Government of Venezuela incl. PDVSA and central bank - escalation from sectoral to near-total embargo. DRAFT coding.

title: G7 price cap on Russian petroleum products takes effect
description: Second-stage cap: $100/bbl premium products and $45/bbl discount products on seaborne Russian diesel/fuel oil, atop the December crude cap. DRAFT coding.

title: US sanctions Gazprom Neft Surgutneftegas and 183 shadow-fleet tankers
description: Largest tanker-sanctions action ever: OFAC hits two major producers plus 183 vessels incl. 69 Sovcomflot ships - direct strike at Russian export logistics. DRAFT coding.

title: IEA coordinated 60M bbl release after Katrina
description: All 26 IEA members offer 60M barrels over 30 days after Katrina wrecks Gulf production - second coordinated release in IEA history. DRAFT coding.

title: IEA coordinated 60M bbl release (Libya disruption)
description: Third-ever coordinated release: 60M barrels (30M US SPR) answering the Libyan outage - the buffer used as designed. DRAFT coding.

title: US-led six-nation coordinated SPR release (50M bbl)
description: First price-motivated coordinated release: US 50M with China India Japan Korea UK - buffers deployed against price not outage. DRAFT coding.

title: US announces record 180M bbl SPR release
description: Largest SPR release in history: 1M bbl/day for six months against the invasion price spike. Exactly 35 days after the invasion - clusters under keep-first rule; flagged. DRAFT coding.
